title: 3D Neural Graph component for React
description: Interactive perspective node graph with connected 3D positions, animated data flow, clusters, selection, and camera controls.

intro: Visualize AI systems, dependencies, and knowledge networks as nodes in three-dimensional space. Connections, clusters, and data-flow pulses make structure and direction easy to explore.

faqs.question: Does Neural Graph need a 3D runtime?
faqs.answer: No. It projects 3D node coordinates onto a canvas, so orbit, pan, and zoom work without an extra peer dependency.

faqs.question: How can I supply a large graph?
faqs.answer: Pass nodes, edges, and clusters as arrays to avoid creating thousands of React child elements. Canvas drawing keeps the DOM small; performance depends on graph density and device hardware.

faqs.question: Can users navigate without a pointer?
faqs.answer: Yes. Focus the graph, use arrow keys to select nodes, plus or minus to zoom, and Escape to clear selection. Reduced-motion preferences disable data-flow animation.

sections.heading: What it does
sections.body: Neural Graph renders nodes and connections on a canvas using perspective projection of x, y, and z coordinates. Nodes have spherical shading and depth ordering.

sections.heading: Camera and selection
sections.body: Drag to orbit, Shift-drag to pan, and scroll or use the toolbar to zoom. Hover and selection highlight connected edges; selection supports controlled and uncontrolled state.

sections.heading: Data and clustering
sections.body: Use ZuiNode, ZuiEdge, and ZuiCluster as declarative children or pass nodes, edges, and clusters arrays for larger data sets. Edges with unknown endpoints are ignored.

sections.heading: Accessibility and motion
sections.body: The graph has a keyboard-focusable region and a live selection status. Arrow keys step through nodes. Animated edge pulses respect reduced-motion preferences.
